## Purpose

This notebook converts the count data models chapter into Python. Main tools:

- `pandas`
- `numpy`
- `statsmodels`
- `geopandas`
- `matplotlib`

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
```

## Read AHRF data

```{python}
import io, zipfile, requests
url = "https://data.hrsa.gov/DataDownload/AHRF/AHRF_2019-2020_SAS.zip"
r = requests.get(url, timeout=120)
z = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(r.content))
name = [n for n in z.namelist() if n.endswith(".sas7bdat")][0]
ahrf = pd.read_sas(z.open(name), format="sas7bdat", encoding="latin1")
ahrf.head()
```

## Recode variables

```{python}
ahrf2 = (
    ahrf.assign(
        cofips=ahrf["f00004"].astype(str),
        coname=ahrf["f00010"],
        state=ahrf["f00011"],
        popn=ahrf["f1198416"],
        births1618=ahrf["f1254616"],
        lowbw1618=ahrf["f1255316"],
        fampov14=ahrf["f1443214"],
        lbrate1618=1000 * (ahrf["f1255316"] / ahrf["f1254616"]),
        rucc=ahrf["f0002013"].astype("category"),
        obgyn15_pc=1000 * (ahrf["f1168415"] / ahrf["f1198416"]),
    )[["births1618", "lowbw1618", "lbrate1618", "state", "cofips", "coname", "popn", "fampov14", "rucc", "obgyn15_pc"]]
    .dropna()
    .copy()
)
ahrf2.head()
```

## Histogram of the low birth weight rate

```{python}
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
plt.hist(ahrf2["lbrate1618"], bins=30)
plt.title("Distribution of low birth weight rates in US counties")
plt.xlabel("Rate per 1,000 live births")
plt.ylabel("Frequency")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Gaussian GLM

```{python}
glm1 = smf.glm("lbrate1618 ~ fampov14 + C(rucc)", data=ahrf2, family=sm.families.Gaussian()).fit()
print(glm1.summary())
```

```{python}
glm2 = smf.glm("lbrate1618 ~ fampov14 + C(rucc)", data=ahrf2, family=sm.families.Gaussian(link=sm.families.links.log())).fit()
print({"AIC_identity": glm1.aic, "AIC_log": glm2.aic})
```

## Binomial regression for grouped events

```{python}
ahrf2["lowbw_prop"] = ahrf2["lowbw1618"] / ahrf2["births1618"]
glmb = smf.glm(
    "lowbw_prop ~ fampov14 + C(rucc)",
    data=ahrf2,
    family=sm.families.Binomial(),
    freq_weights=ahrf2["births1618"]
).fit()
print(glmb.summary())
```

```{python}
np.exp(glmb.params)
```

## Poisson rate model with offset

```{python}
glmp = smf.glm(
    "lowbw1618 ~ fampov14 + C(rucc)",
    data=ahrf2,
    family=sm.families.Poisson(),
    offset=np.log(ahrf2["births1618"])
).fit()
print(glmp.summary())
np.exp(glmp.params)
```

## Check overdispersion

```{python}
scale = glmp.deviance / glmp.df_resid
scale
```

## Robust covariance alternative

```{python}
glmp_robust = smf.glm(
    "lowbw1618 ~ fampov14 + C(rucc)",
    data=ahrf2,
    family=sm.families.Poisson(),
    offset=np.log(ahrf2["births1618"])
).fit(cov_type="HC1")
print(glmp_robust.summary())
```

## Negative binomial model

```{python}
glmnb = smf.glm(
    "lowbw1618 ~ fampov14 + C(rucc)",
    data=ahrf2,
    family=sm.families.NegativeBinomial(),
    offset=np.log(ahrf2["births1618"])
).fit()
print(glmnb.summary())
np.exp(glmnb.params)
```

## Fractional logit substitute for beta style outcomes

```{python}
ahrf2["lbrate_prop"] = ahrf2["lbrate1618"] / 1000
fraclogit = smf.glm(
    "lbrate_prop ~ fampov14 + C(rucc)",
    data=ahrf2.loc[(ahrf2["lbrate_prop"] > 0) & (ahrf2["lbrate_prop"] < 1)],
    family=sm.families.Binomial()
).fit()
print(fraclogit.summary())
```

## Notes

- `statsmodels` covers Gaussian, binomial, Poisson, and negative binomial very well
- Grouped binomial models in Python usually use proportions plus `freq_weights`
- Negative binomial is the main Python replacement when Poisson overdispersion is substantial
